input_status.Elo: tested clean for data flow: scores after the cutoff were corrupted and the Elo-based features did not move (lab perturbation audit, four weeks plus 2025 week 10). Not tested: whether the Elo constants were tuned on outcomes that include later games.
input_status.EPA aggregates: tested clean for data flow: play aggregates after the cutoff were replaced with noise and the EPA edges did not move. Not tested: the play-value model behind EPA is trained on many seasons at once (from memory, small but real).
input_status.ESPN FPI: not testable here: FPI is fetched live at freeze time (homewin_eval.fpi_projection) and no historical snapshots exist, so a past-week value cannot be checked for revision. Treat any FPI value not archived at the time as unusable for backtests.
input_status.FantasyPoints files: not tested in this protocol: they feed the props pipeline (FPDS), not the winner, spread or total features this audit covers. The adapter note says files describe the previous week; that week mapping needs its own file-level check.
input_status.hourly Kalshi candles: tested: candle ts is Kalshi's end_period_ts (lab/kalshi.py lines 155 to 167), corrupting candles after the cutoff left the price at the cutoff unchanged, and corrupting up to cutoff plus 1 hour changed it (planted_candle_leak).
input_status.ESPN injury snapshots: tested in part: the lab's injury table (available_at) was corrupted after the cutoff without moving features. The raw ESPN snapshot files under data/raw/archive were not separately perturbed; their file names carry a UTC time but a later snapshot can rewrite statuses, so only the snapshot at or before the cutoff may be used.
